claim: Compile result separates semantic order, device execution state, memory proof, queues, grouping, dispatches, fences, and search diagnostics.
Scheduling and timing defaults, hard memory budget, frames in flight, search modes, and adaptive configuration.
Search and stable ordering validate topological order; configured search produces and publishes order diagnostics.
Greedy critical and memory ordering, bounded local candidate improvement, and iterative exhaustive/backtracking search.
Build allocation lifetimes, evaluate serialization policies, preserve alias dependencies, estimate queue makespan and domain/alias penalties, rank candidates.
Queue placement requires device support and legal states, sufficient compute chain and independent graphics slack, includes memory edges; CUDA runs ignore declarations.
Memory requests, native requirements, heap restrictions, alias activations, accounting across frame pools, and describe/plan/materialize separation.

Imports and persistent resources retained, outputs persistent for allocation, retained adapter workspace accounted, synthetic scratch and CUDA placement restrictions, hard caps require native device requirements.
Pending physical plan materialization stages ownership and can retry; cold persistent initialization waits; per-frame pools, bindings, and lowering prepare before runtime publication.
Dispatches bind actual physical resources; aliases insert image activation/retirement; CUDA and acceleration-structure commands record at submit time.
Batch compatibility includes pipeline and framebuffer format, queues, memory boundaries, and access hazards; not general shader fusion.
Batches partition executable nodes, one CUDA framework stream, fence resolution contracts declarations and includes memory edges and per-domain chains.
CUDA operand access, state, byte ranges and texture mip/layer footprint must be covered by current node declarations.
Instancing candidates require all stage opt-in, compatible logical bindings and targets, no other storage effects or unsupported per-node state.
Native merge checks pipeline, bindings, framebuffer, geometry, viewport/scissor, draw parameters and contiguous non-overflowing instance ranges.
Tests verify explicit stage permission, resource differences and storage effects prevent merge, and preserve noncontiguous/reset instances and native state changes.
Private command program stores already bound resources and recording/dependency/state products, not authoring/allocation/culling/scheduling.
Finalization merges read requirements, tracks texture cells and whole-buffer states, emits barriers and entry/exit sentinel plan.
Physical identities drive continuity; queue ownership transfer introduces release/acquire and dependencies, while UAV buffer barriers consider overlap and writes.
Equal-state exit transitions preserve ownership transfer and aliased image retirements define reusable boundary.
Independent recording uses bounded CPU jobs while deterministic submission honors queue tokens and retains accepted work after partial failure.
Execution result includes status, counts, submission tokens, dependencies, and independently observed state/ownership conformance.
Executor validates successful plan, atomically claims execution ownership, retains cloned compiled input and delegates execution.
Standalone compile result survives source destruction, preserves input, rejects second executor claiming copied plan, and device-independent plans cannot execute GPU work.
Native callbacks fulfill promises; draining publishes in compiled pass order and clears all pending destinations on any failure.
Readback tests cover delayed publication, destroyed unsubmitted callbacks, partial submission drainage, and all-output invalidation.

Submit may wait for pool reuse, returns tickets for partial failure, serializes shared inter-frame ownership, Wait retires accepted work and publishes readbacks, and IsComplete polls without draining.
Ticket completion identity and retained report, device, tokens, readbacks and telemetry are independent of reusable frame slot.
Lifecycle tests defer tuning until retirement, reject obsolete telemetry epochs, retry failed materialization, retain receipts, and avoid device idle and blocking polling.
Timing aggregate/individual distinctions, collection-order EMA, latest frame fields, bounded raw node history, and modeled adaptive statistics.
Measured-region attribution, immutable background snapshots, pool reuse, revision/epoch validity, retirement-gated adoption and explicit cancellation.
EMA, stable node identity keys, collection-order handling, bounded individual-node history, and epoch reset.
Adaptive tests cover bounded progress, hysteresis, preserving fixed alias/budget constraints, workspace allocation reuse and proportional batch attribution.
Timing cost override applies only when node name, canonical key, and executable definition match; declarations cost zero.
Frame slot owns physical memory, lowered commands, per-node bindings, timer state and CUDA caches; reusable-frame record retains pools for adaptation.
Device ownership and mutable runtime/caches/timing are stored separately from authored topology and execution ownership is single-claim.
D3D12 queues a GPU-side wait for the producer timeline value.
Vulkan submits a timeline-semaphore wait to the consumer queue.
The generic QueueWait fallback uses host completion waiting; providers may override it.
